nodes.label: graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: graphify query/path/explain return scoped subgraphs far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep; the committed graph.json is rewritten whole on every build so a large PR diff is expected.

nodes.label: Lazy OpenAI Client via app.llm.get_client()
nodes.rationale: The client is built lazily so importing any module never requires an API key; OPENAI_BASE_URL lets the same code target any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

nodes.label: Three Shared LLM Patterns (Structured Output, Tool Loop, RAG)
nodes.norm_label: three shared llm patterns (structured output, tool loop, rag)

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled Agent Loop (research_lead)
nodes.rationale: The bounded for-loop with early break plus a final structured-output call is the same pattern every agent framework builds on, written explicitly instead of hidden in a library.

nodes.label: Source:Index Citation Tagging
nodes.rationale: ASK_SYSTEM_PROMPT forces answers only from provided context and cites [source:index], which is what reduces hallucination.

nodes.label: Environment-Only Configuration (app/config.py)
nodes.rationale: Every module imports from config instead of reading os.environ, so switching provider or database only means editing .env.

nodes.label: ingest_docs Ingestion Pipeline
nodes.rationale: No duplicate check exists, so running the script twice inserts every chunk twice; it only appends rows.

nodes.label: Mocked Enrichment Tools (Acme Corp / Globex)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded dicts stand in for real Apollo/Clay/HubSpot calls; any other company name returns "Unknown" values.

nodes.label: pgvector Cosine Distance Search (<=>)
nodes.rationale: Retrieval is one SQL query over doc_chunks ordered by the <=> cosine-distance operator; EMBEDDING_DIM = 1536 is tied to text-embedding-3-small so changing the model means changing the schema.

nodes.label: Pydantic Request/Response Contracts
nodes.rationale: Schemas act as contracts so FastAPI rejects malformed requests before user code runs; QualifyResponse is reused as the AI response_format.

nodes.label: Thin Router Request Flow
nodes.rationale: Request flow is app/main.py -> app/routers/* (thin, one call each) -> logic in llm.py, rag/qa.py or agent/loop.py, keeping routers logic-free.

nodes.label: Structured Output (parse with response_format)
nodes.rationale: client.beta.chat.completions.parse(response_format=PydanticModel) forces the model into a strict JSON shape; a None parse result is treated as a refusal and raises ValueError.

nodes.label: Tool-Calling Loop (_AVAILABLE_TOOLS dispatch)
nodes.rationale: The model only requests tools; local code resolves the name through a _AVAILABLE_TOOLS name-to-function dict, runs it, and appends a role:"tool" message, repeating up to max_turns.

nodes.label: Known Gaps: No Reranking, No Auth
nodes.norm_label: known gaps: no reranking, no auth
nodes.rationale: The RAG pipeline is intentionally the simplest working baseline (no reranking or metadata filtering) and the API has no authentication or rate limiting because it is a learning project.

nodes.label: Deployment on Railway or Fly.io
nodes.rationale: Both routes need a Postgres+pgvector instance and the user's own account credentials; deploying is left to the operator.

nodes.label: Secrets Hygiene via Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: Secrets come only from environment variables through app/config.py; .env is git-ignored and .env.example documents what is needed without real values.

nodes.label: Deliberate Exclusion of Agent Frameworks
nodes.rationale: LangChain and other agent frameworks are left out on purpose so the code can be read top-to-bottom; adding them is explicitly discouraged.

nodes.label: Router-Level Monkeypatch Test Strategy
nodes.rationale: Tests monkeypatch the function as imported into the router module (e.g. app.routers.ask.rag_ask) rather than where it is defined, so no network, API key or database is needed.

nodes.label: Duplicated Tool Loops in llm.py and agent/loop.py
nodes.norm_label: duplicated tool loops in llm.py and agent/loop.py
nodes.rationale: The two tool loops are separate copies kept for readability; a change to one must be checked against the other.

nodes.label: Paragraph-Aware Chunking with Overlap
nodes.rationale: Chunks must be small enough to be relevant yet overlap enough (~100 chars, ~800 char windows) that an answer is not split across a boundary.

nodes.label: Learn Raw Fundamentals Before Frameworks
nodes.rationale: Building the raw tool-calling loop and raw RAG pipeline makes debugging framework-based agents easier later, since frameworks like LangGraph merely wrap exactly this loop.

nodes.label: Mock Tools Are Isolated Swap Points
nodes.norm_label: mock tools are isolated swap points
nodes.rationale: Replacing the mocks with real Apollo/Clay/HubSpot HTTP calls would only touch _lookup_company_firmographics and _search_company_info; nothing else in the loop changes.

nodes.label: Prompt Engineering for Reliability, Not Cleverness
nodes.norm_label: prompt engineering for reliability, not cleverness
nodes.rationale: Every system prompt exists to constrain output format and behavior (score range, answer only from context, call the tool at most once), which is what production prompt engineering mostly is.

nodes.label: README Design Notes (Why It's Built This Way)
nodes.norm_label: readme design notes (why it's built this way)
nodes.rationale: Structured outputs, tool use, hand-built RAG and env-only secrets are chosen so every abstraction is readable top to bottom rather than hidden in a framework.
